text: There is no direct evidence in the current PubMed literature supporting a functional interaction between the ACE inhibitor Lisinopril and the ERBB2 (HER2) receptor in the context of breast cancer. Mechanistically, Lisinopril is a highly specific inhibitor of Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme (ACE) and lacks known structural affinity for the ERBB2 tyrosine kinase domain. While some studies suggest that the Renin-Angiotensin System (RAS) can influence tumor microenvironments, any potential link between Lisinopril and HER2-positive breast cancer would likely be indirect, involving systemic hemodynamic changes or modulation of downstream signaling pathways rather than direct target binding [PMID: 25603365]. Consequently, Lisinopril is not considered a therapeutic agent for targeting ERBB2 in clinical oncology.
